botanical_pharmacopoeia.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
botanical_pharmacopoeia.license: Official Statutory Pharmacopoeial Standards (PCIM&H / Ministry of AYUSH)

nutrition_pathya.publisher: ICMR - National Institute of Nutrition (NIN) & Ministry of AYUSH
nutrition_pathya.license: Public Health Guidance / Open Clinical Reference

clinical_safety_referral.name: Clinical Safety, Contraindications & Red-Flag Escalation
clinical_safety_referral.description: Herb-drug interaction matrices, AYUSH Pharmacovigilance criteria, maternal/pediatric safety, and emergency red-flag symptoms.
clinical_safety_referral.publisher: National Pharmacovigilance Centre (NPvCC), AIIA & Ministry of AYUSH

documents.title: Charaka Saṃhitā: Definition of Svastha, Ayu, and Tridosha Equilibrium
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (National Institute of Indian Medical Heritage / Ministry of AYUSH)
documents.license: Public Domain (Classical Sanskrit Literature; Digitized via Government Open Access)
documents.relevance: Core definition of holistic health (Svastha), foundational Tridosha balance criteria, and Agni equilibrium.
documents.limitations: Philosophical foundation requiring contextual translation; not a substitute for modern clinical diagnostic lab metrics.

documents.title: Charaka Saṃhitā: Daily Regimen (Dinacharya) & Dietary Measure (Matrashitiya)
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Caraka / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Provides circadian daily scheduling, food portioning, and preventive hygienic practices.
documents.limitations: Individual adjustments required based on geographical location (Desha) and patient occupation.

documents.title: Charaka Saṃhitā: Seasonal Regimens (Ritucharya) & Environmental Adaptation
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Caraka / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Critical for seasonal diet adaptation and explaining how environmental transitions aggravate specific doshas.
documents.limitations: Classical 6-season division (Ritus) must be mapped to regional temperate or tropical zones.

documents.title: Charaka Saṃhitā: Non-Suppressible Natural Urges (Adharaniya Vega) & Disease Etiology
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Caraka / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Directly links modern lifestyle habits (holding urine, bowel movements, skipping meals) to Vata disorders.
documents.limitations: Suppression consequences need correlation with contemporary functional gastrointestinal and autonomic disorders.

documents.title: Charaka Saṃhitā: Properties, Functions, and Pathological Manifestations of Vata
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Caraka / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Crucial for understanding Vata phenotypes, neurological excitability, musculoskeletal pain, and cold intolerance.
documents.limitations: Describes systemic manifestations that require modern differential diagnosis to rule out organic neurological disorders.

documents.title: Charaka Saṃhitā: Wholesome & Unwholesome Foods and Premier Substances (Agrya Dravyas)
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Caraka / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Provides gold-standard dietary recommendations (Pathya) and authoritative single-herb hierarchies.
documents.limitations: Some ancient animal preparations mentioned in the chapter are historical; current application focuses on plant and dairy agrya dravyas.

documents.title: Charaka Saṃhitā: Comprehensive Dietetics & Nutritional Classification (Annapanavidhi)
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Caraka / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Underpins the nutritional recommendation engine for customized food lists.
documents.limitations: Requires integration with modern nutrient content metrics (calories, protein, glycemic index).

documents.title: Charaka Saṃhitā: The Eight Factors of Dietetics (Aṣṭāvidha Āhāravidhi Viśeṣāyatana)
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Caraka / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Provides behavioral eating rules (mindful eating, eating warm, fresh, unhurried meals) in personalized plans.
documents.limitations: Focuses on digestive psychology; must be accompanied by nutrient adequacy checks.

documents.title: Charaka Saṃhitā: Tenfold Clinical Examination of the Patient (Daśavidha Parīkṣā)
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Caraka / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: The direct clinical foundation for AyuRAG-XAI's multi-factorial assessment model.
documents.limitations: Comprehensive clinical pariksha requires physical tactile and visual examination by a qualified physician.

documents.title: Charaka Saṃhitā: Pathophysiology of Agni, Ama, and Grahani Disorders
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Caraka / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Direct clinical reference for Agni classification (Sama, Vishama, Tikshna, Manda) and digestive recommendations.
documents.limitations: Chronic malabsorption disorders and inflammatory bowel disease require modern gastroenterological endoscopy and testing.

documents.title: Suśruta Saṃhitā: Clinical Signs of Increase and Decrease of Doshas, Dhatus, and Malas
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (National Institute of Indian Medical Heritage / AYUSH)
documents.relevance: Provides objective clinical symptom indicators for dosha and tissue depletion or excess.
documents.limitations: Tissue depletion (Dhatu Kshaya) symptoms should be correlated with biochemical laboratory markers (e.g. CBC, ferritin).

documents.title: Suśruta Saṃhitā: The Six Stages of Disease Progression (Ṣaṭ Kriyākāla)
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Sushruta / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Provides chronological clinical stages, demonstrating that preventive intervention in early stages halts disease progression.
documents.limitations: Stages 5 and 6 (Bhedavastha) indicate manifest anatomical disease requiring medical or surgical intervention.

documents.title: Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdayam: Core Foundations of Health & Tridosha Dynamics (Āyuṣkāmīya)
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Ashtanga / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Defines the fundamental axioms of Ayurvedic treatment: like increases like, opposites cure.
documents.limitations: Axiomatic rules require personalized calibration based on metabolic rate and clinical contraindications.

documents.title: Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdayam: Circadian Daily Regimen & Preventive Self-Care (Dinacharya)
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Ashtanga / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Provides the blueprint for personalized daily circadian schedules generated by AyuRAG-XAI.
documents.limitations: Waking hours and exercise intensity must be adapted for shift-workers and individuals with chronic illness.

documents.title: Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdayam: Incompatible Food Combinations & Toxic Synergies (Viruddhāhāra)
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Ashtanga / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Crucial for generating dietary contraindications and warning users against harmful food combinations.
documents.limitations: Mechanisms of toxicity reflect classical physiological perspectives; contemporary verification is documented for specific allergies and enzymatic mismatches.

documents.title: Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdayam: Stomach Volumetric Division for Optimal Digestion
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Ashtanga / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Direct guideline for meal portioning and preventing postprandial bloating or indigestion.
documents.limitations: Provides qualitative volume estimation; must be paired with individualized caloric requirements.

documents.title: CCRAS: General Guidelines for Clinical Evaluation of Ayurvedic Interventions
documents.publisher: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS), Ministry of AYUSH, Govt. of India
documents.license: Open Government Data (OGD) - India / Research and Academic Fair Use
documents.download_availability: Publicly accessible via ccras.nic.in document archive
documents.relevance: Provides the methodological benchmark for evaluating clinical Ayurvedic decision support and avoiding unscientific claims.
documents.limitations: Focuses on trial design protocols rather than automated software algorithms; adapted for clinical software validation.

documents.title: CCRAS: Standardized Technical Protocol for Deha Prakriti Assessment
documents.publisher: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS)
documents.publication_version: CCRAS Technical Protocol, Validated Assessment Tool
documents.relevance: Direct algorithmic reference for AyuRAG-XAI's Prakriti questionnaire scoring and constitutional classification.
documents.limitations: Self-reported questionnaires carry cognitive bias; doctor clinical verification remains necessary for definitive typing.

documents.title: CCRAS: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Digestive Fire (Agni) Evaluation
documents.publisher: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS)
documents.relevance: Provides objective clinical diagnostic symptoms for determining patient Agni status in AyuRAG-XAI.
documents.limitations: Subjective symptom clusters; should be supported by dietary recall and stool frequency logging.

documents.title: CCRAS Clinical Practice Guideline: Management of Amavata (Rheumatoid Spectrum)
documents.publisher: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS)
documents.relevance: Provides evidence-based lifestyle, nutrition, and referral guidance for joint inflammation and systemic stiffness.
documents.limitations: Aggressive erosive joint disease requires ongoing rheumatological monitoring, anti-CCP/RF titers, and safe co-management.

documents.title: CCRAS Clinical Practice Guideline: Lifestyle & Dietary Protocol for Madhumeha (Type 2 Diabetes)
documents.publisher: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS)
documents.relevance: Provides authoritative guidance for metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, and blood sugar regulation.
documents.limitations: Does not replace allopathic insulin in Type 1 diabetes or acute diabetic ketoacidosis; HbA1c monitoring mandatory.

documents.title: CCRAS Clinical Practice Guideline: Management of Amlapitta (Hyperacidity & GERD)
documents.publisher: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS)
documents.relevance: Provides non-pharmacological and herbal management for heartburn, gastric burning, and acid regurgitation.
documents.limitations: Gastric ulcer perforation or persistent hematemesis requires immediate emergency allopathic care.

documents.title: CCRAS Clinical Practice Guideline: Management of Anidra (Primary Insomnia)
documents.publisher: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS)
documents.relevance: Evidence-based non-pharmacological protocols for sleep disturbances, nighttime restlessness, and stress.
documents.limitations: Severe psychiatric depression, bipolar disorder, or obstructive sleep apnea require specialized medical review.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Withania somnifera (Ashwagandha)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H), Ministry of AYUSH
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 08
documents.license: Official Government Statutory Standard (PCIM&H / Ministry of AYUSH)
documents.download_availability: Official publication via pcimh.gov.in / National Portal
documents.relevance: Authoritative standard for Ashwagandha identification, indications, dosage, and safety contraindications.
documents.limitations: Monograph covers root material; extracts with high withanolide standardization require clinical dose titration.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Tinospora cordifolia (Guduchi/Giloy)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 17
documents.relevance: Authoritative reference for immune modulation, fever management, and metabolic detoxification.
documents.limitations: Rare idiosyncratic hepatotoxicity reported with adulterated species (Tinospora crispa); authentic T. cordifolia verified.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Phyllanthus emblica (Amalaki/Amla)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 04
documents.relevance: Premier antioxidant, digestive balancer, and Pitta-pacifying fruit monograph.
documents.limitations: High raw acidity may cause mild transient heartburn in sensitive individuals if taken on completely empty stomach.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Terminalia chebula (Haritaki)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 19
documents.relevance: Premier bowel regulator, gut detoxifier, and Triphala component.
documents.limitations: Contraindicated in severe dehydration, acute exhaustion, and pregnancy.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Asparagus racemosus (Shatavari)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. IV, Monograph 35
documents.relevance: Premier reproductive tonic, gastric mucosal protector, and cooling Pitta-Vata balancer.
documents.limitations: Caution in estrogen-receptor positive hormone-sensitive neoplasms; monitor in severe fluid retention.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Bacopa monnieri (Brahmi)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. II, Monograph 08
documents.relevance: Premier neuroprotective, cognitive enhancing (Medhya), and anxiolytic botanical.
documents.limitations: Can cause mild gastrointestinal cramping or nausea when consumed on an empty stomach.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Commiphora mukul (Guggulu)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 18
documents.relevance: Premier lipid-modulating, anti-inflammatory, and anti-arthritic gum resin.
documents.limitations: Must undergo traditional Sodhana purification; contra-indicated with anticoagulant drugs.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Zingiber officinale (Shunthi/Ginger)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 62
documents.relevance: Universal digestive stimulant (Vishvabheshaja), carminative, and Ama-digestant.
documents.limitations: Excessive intake can provoke burning in active ulcerative gastritis or acute bleeding hemorrhoids.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Ocimum sanctum (Tulsi)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. II, Monograph 67
documents.relevance: Premier respiratory adaptogen, antimicrobial, and Kapha-Vata balancing herb.
documents.limitations: Mild anti-fertility effects demonstrated in high-dose animal models; use in moderation during conception efforts.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Curcuma longa (Haridra/Turmeric)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 22
documents.relevance: Premier anti-inflammatory, dermal tonic, blood purifier, and metabolic adjuvant.
documents.limitations: High-dose curcumin extracts contraindicated in mechanical gallstone obstruction; enhances antiplatelet drugs.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Glycyrrhiza glabra (Yashtimadhu/Licorice)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 61
documents.relevance: Premier mucosal protector, demulcent, and Pitta-Vata pacifier.
documents.limitations: Prolonged high doses (>6 weeks) can induce pseudoaldosteronism, hypokalemia, and secondary hypertension.

documents.title: ICMR-NIN 2024: Dietary Guidelines for Indians (17 Core Public Health Directives)
documents.publisher: National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN), Indian Council of Medical Research
documents.publication_version: Dietary Guidelines for Indians, Revised 2024 Edition
documents.license: Public Health Guidance (ICMR-NIN, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare)
documents.relevance: Modern evidence-based nutrition framework governing healthy diets and chronic disease prevention.
documents.limitations: National population level recommendations requiring clinical personalization for individual metabolic profiles.

documents.title: Clinical Pathya-Apathya Food Selection Matrix for Constitutional Dosha Imbalances
documents.publisher: AyuRAG Clinical Knowledge Curation / CCRAS and ICMR-NIN Cross-Validated Standards
documents.download_availability: Publicly accessible via AYUSH Research Portal / AyuRAG Knowledge Base
documents.relevance: Provides exact food recommendations (Pathya) and foods to avoid (Apathya) for Vata, Pitta, and Kapha.
documents.limitations: Individual food tolerances (Satmya) and culinary food allergies supersede broad group classifications.

documents.title: Classical Principles of Food Transformation (Āhāra Pariṇāmakara Bhāva)
documents.publisher: AyuRAG Clinical Knowledge Base / Charaka Saṃhitā Sharirasthana Ch 6
documents.relevance: Explains how the six factors of metabolism digest food into healthy tissues rather than inflammatory Ama.
documents.limitations: Philosophical physiological concepts that parallel gastrointestinal motility, enzymes, and temperature.

documents.title: Ministry of AYUSH: National Pharmacovigilance Program for ASU&H Drugs & ADR Guidelines
documents.publisher: National Pharmacovigilance Coordination Centre (NPvCC), All India Institute of Ayurveda & Ministry of AYUSH
documents.license: Open Government Data (OGD) - India / Public Clinical Safety Guidance
documents.relevance: Provides the safety foundation: natural does not automatically equal safe; mandates ADR monitoring.
documents.limitations: Post-market spontaneous reporting framework; under-reporting of mild ADRs is a documented global limitation.

documents.title: Clinical Red-Flag Symptoms & Immediate Allopathic Emergency Referral Escalation Protocol
documents.publisher: AyuRAG Clinical Safety Board / Integrated Critical Care Guidelines
documents.publication_version: Clinical Decision Support Safety Standard v3.1, 2024
documents.download_availability: Publicly accessible via AyuRAG Knowledge Portal
documents.relevance: Essential clinical safety guardrail: immediately flags life-threatening red-flag symptoms for urgent emergency referral.
documents.limitations: Algorithmic screening protocol; cannot replace physical bedside emergency triage by a licensed physician.

documents.title: Clinical Herb-Drug Interaction Matrix: Key Ayurvedic Botanicals & Modern Pharmaceuticals
documents.publisher: AyuRAG Clinical Pharmacology Working Group / AYUSH Suraksha Pharmacovigilance Cross-Index
documents.relevance: Protects patients taking concurrent modern prescription medications from adverse herb-drug interactions.
documents.limitations: In vitro and animal cytochrome P450 modulation data require ongoing clinical confirmation in human trials.

documents.title: Clinical Safety Guidance: Botanical Contraindications in Pregnancy and Lactation
documents.publisher: Ministry of AYUSH & CCRAS Mother and Child Health Guidelines
documents.relevance: Strict safety filtering to exclude abortifacient, emmenagogue, or uterine stimulant herbs in pregnant users.
documents.limitations: Ethical constraints preclude randomized trials in pregnant women; cautious avoidance principle strictly applied.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia Standards for Sodhana (Purification / Detoxification Protocols)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: Ayurvedic Formulary of India (AFI) & API Part-I Appendices
documents.relevance: Explains why unpurified poisonous herbs are strictly toxic and how classical processing detoxifies raw materials.
documents.limitations: Industrial manufacturing compliance requires lab verification of alkaloid/heavy-metal reduction.

documents.title: Charaka Saṃhitā: Science of Rejuvenation & Immunological Longevity (Rasāyana)
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Caraka / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Underpins preventive lifestyle guidelines, cellular longevity, and Ojas enhancement.
documents.limitations: Classical internal purification (Panchakarma) prerequisite must be adapted for modern outpatient settings.

documents.title: Charaka Saṃhitā: Management of Fever, Agni Restoration, and Langhana Therapy
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Caraka / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Provides protocols for managing acute digestive shutdown, metabolic fever, and therapeutic fasting.
documents.limitations: Severe bacterial sepsis, high persistent fever (>39°C), and pediatric febrile convulsions require immediate allopathic hospital admission.

documents.title: Suśruta Saṃhitā: Water Quality, Beverage Thermodynamics, and Meal Rhythm
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Sushruta / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Direct guideline for water temperature, meal timing, and drinking water during meals.
documents.limitations: Ancient water collection terms (rain vs pond water) must be mapped to modern filtered, potable water standards.

documents.title: Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdayam: Seasonal Transitions (Ṛtucaryā) & Seasonal Sandhi Care
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Ashtanga / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Explains Ritu Sandhi (the 14-day transitional junction between seasons) and why acute illnesses spike during seasonal changes.
documents.limitations: Requires alignment with local meteorology and geographical hemisphere.

documents.title: Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdayam: Physiological Functions of Balanced Doshas and Tissues
documents.publisher: Classical Ayurvedic Compendium (e-Ashtanga / NIIMH)
documents.relevance: Provides the normal physiological benchmark against which patient symptoms are compared.
documents.limitations: Qualitative functional observations; must be correlated with contemporary vital signs and organ function tests.

documents.title: CCRAS Clinical Practice Guideline: Management of Sthaulya (Obesity & Dyslipidemia)
documents.publisher: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS)
documents.relevance: Authoritative dietary and lifestyle management for elevated BMI, visceral adiposity, and sluggish metabolism.
documents.limitations: Severe morbid obesity with sleep apnea or endocrine tumors (Cushing's) requires specialized endocrinological workup.

documents.title: CCRAS Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Guidelines for Ayurvedic Clinical Research
documents.publisher: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS)
documents.relevance: Governs data integrity, patient informed consent, and adverse event reporting in clinical systems.
documents.limitations: Institutional standard requiring local institutional ethics committee (IEC) oversight for human subjects.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Azadirachta indica (Nimba/Neem)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. II, Monograph 53
documents.relevance: Premier bitter blood purifier, antimicrobial, and Pitta-Kapha pacifying leaf/bark.
documents.limitations: Prolonged high doses can aggravate Vata, cause emaciation, and exert mild anti-spermatogenic effects.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Tribulus terrestris (Gokshura)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 16
documents.relevance: Premier nephroprotective, lithotriptic, and rejuvenating diuretic tonic.
documents.limitations: Caution in patients taking modern synthetic potassium-sparing diuretics to prevent hyperkalemia.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Boerhavia diffusa (Punarnava)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 47
documents.relevance: Premier anti-edematous, diuretic, and hepatoprotective whole plant.
documents.limitations: In end-stage renal disease (ESRD) requiring dialysis, fluid volume and potassium must be managed under nephrology care.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Boswellia serrata (Shallaki)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. IV, Monograph 41
documents.relevance: Premier botanical for osteoarthritis, inflammatory joint disease, and cartilage preservation.
documents.limitations: May cause mild gastric discomfort or acid reflux in sensitive individuals if taken without food.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Andrographis paniculata (Kalmegh/Bhunimba)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. II, Monograph 10
documents.relevance: Premier hepatoprotective, bitter febrifuge, and upper respiratory infection botanical.
documents.limitations: Very intense bitter taste; high doses can cause loss of appetite, nausea, or allergic rash.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Piper nigrum (Maricha/Black Pepper)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. III, Monograph 17
documents.relevance: Key bioavailability enhancer (piperine), respiratory mucolytic, and Trikatu component.
documents.limitations: Pungent and hot; excessive consumption aggravates Pitta and produces gastric burning.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Piper longum (Pippali/Long Pepper)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. IV, Monograph 28
documents.relevance: Premier respiratory rejuvenator (Pranavaha Srotas Rasayana) and digestive stimulant.
documents.limitations: Classical caveat: prolonged continuous usage of Pippali without milk/honey can irritate Pitta.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Cuminum cyminum (Jeeraka/Cumin)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 24
documents.relevance: Premier carminative spice for bloating, abdominal colic, and maternal digestive care.
documents.limitations: Safe culinary herb with virtually no toxicities; therapeutic dosages above 6g daily rarely necessary.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Foeniculum vulgare (Mishreya/Fennel)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 38
documents.relevance: Mild cooling carminative, ideal for infant colic, Pitta indigestion, and postprandial freshening.
documents.limitations: Pure essential oil contains estragole and must not be ingested undiluted; whole seeds safe.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Coriandrum sativum (Dhanyaka/Coriander)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 14
documents.relevance: Premier Pitta-pacifying digestive, thirst quencher, and cooling diuretic.
documents.limitations: Safe culinary spice; no documented toxicities at dietary levels.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Allium sativum (Lashuna/Garlic)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. III, Monograph 22
documents.relevance: Premier Vata-pacifier, cardiovascular lipid regulator, and anti-arthritic bulb.
documents.limitations: Strongly aggravates Pitta; high doses contraindicated with anticoagulants and before surgery.

documents.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Monograph: Elettaria cardamomum (Ela/Cardamom)
documents.publisher: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)
documents.publication_version: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part-I, Vol. I, Monograph 15
documents.relevance: Aromatic digestive, anti-emetic, and refreshing Pitta-Vata carminative.
